newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-IF IT WORKS, WHY FIX IT? JUVENTUS ASK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IF IT WORKS, WHY FIX IT? JUVENTUS ASK.

text.p: "If it works, why fix it?" ask Juventus as they prepare to defend their Italian league title and launch another assault on the European Cup.

With a month to go before the start of the new season, Juve's squad looks reassuringly familiar to the one which dominated serie A last season, reached the final of Europe's premier club competition and won the European and world supercups.
The defence is intact as is much of the midfield. Leading striker Alessandro Del Piero is still there and, although his striking partners have changed, continuity is this summer's theme in Turin.
Even the handful of new Juve recruits will appear familiar to coach Marcello Lippi as he prepares for his fourth season in charge at the Delle Alpe stadium.
Lippi has bought Uruguayan striker Daniel Fonseca from Roma and midfielder Fabio Pecchia from Napoli in the close season. Both men played under him at Napoli in the 1993-94 season.
"Lippi's not changed fundamentally since his days at Napoli," Pecchia said after a training session at Juve's peaceful summer camp in the spectacular Italian Alps.
"He's still the same coach, although maybe he seems a little more experienced, more convinced of his methods."
Pecchia, a compact, combative midfielder who has been widely tipped for an international call-up, said he had two principal targets for next season.
"I want to establish myself in this Juventus side and I want to go with Italy to the World Cup in France," he said.

"Playing for Italy was an impossible dream when I was at Napoli but at Juventus everything is possible. I was a Napoli fan as a young boy but Juventus were always the team that made the biggest impression on me."
For Fonseca, the move to Juventus marks a new beginning after a disappointing 1996-97 campaign in which his form deserted him and his Roma side ended up in the bottom half of the league.
The Uruguayan, who had been at Roma for three years and is preparing for his eighth consecutive season in serie A, said the change of scene had acted as a much-needed tonic.
"I'm finally happy," he said. "I wake up in the morning feeling good and thinking how lucky I am. I've rediscovered the smile which I lost last season.
"I know Lippi well and I'm ready to return to the top level," he said. "Juve haven't changed very much since last season but really there's no need to change."

The few alterations Juventus have made are undoubtably significant. Striker Christian Vieri left for Spain's Atletico Madrid, Croat Alen Boksic returned to Lazio accompanied by Yugoslav midfielder Vladimir Jugovic.

But they have not gone in for the overhauls favoured by the two big Milan sides and Lippi's other new purchase, Filippo Inzaghi, is just the man to provide the goals Vieri and Boksic scored for Juventus last season.
"Everything's going to plan and I'm settling in very well," said Inzaghi, who played last season with Atalanta and was the top scorer in serie A.
"It's a very settled squad and, even after less than a week's training, we're combining well together."
Juventus play English premier league Newcastle in Cesena, near Italy's Adriatic coast, on Sunday. They start their title defence in their centenary year at the end of August.
